maria.khan: Hi team \u2014 urgent question. New hire Ahmed P is due to start Monday but his H-1B stamp appointment got canceled and the next slot is in two weeks. He already has I-797 approval but no visa stamp. Can we have him start remotely from his home country? What documentation does he need to present to payroll/benefits, and how do we handle I-9? cc @anya.ramos

anya.ramos: Sorry to hear about Ahmed's appointment. Short answer: yes, we can allow a short-term remote start in most cases, but there are caveats around payroll and I-9. Steps: 1) collect scans (passport, I-797, DS-160 confirmation, offer), 2) consult immigration counsel about consulate expedite, 3) coordinate I-9 verification with our vendor for remote inspection or authorized representative. We'll need clarity on his intended remote work country for tax implications.

maria.khan: He's in Pakistan currently. Manager asked whether we can ship laptop internationally. Manager prefers laptop shipped and activated when Ahmed confirms arrival back in US. Also asked about benefits effective date if his US-based start date shifts.

oliver.singh: Eng note: onboarding tasks (workspace access, Slack, repo invites) can proceed immediately. We can delay creating cloud credentials with MFA until he completes device enrollment. For laptop shipping: use asset tag "hold-until-activation" and require manager sign-off for activation.

diane.park: Payroll/Benefits: If Ahmed's payroll start date remains the original hire date, benefits eligibility will begin as scheduled. If we push payroll start beyond 30 days, benefits enrollment windows may need manual re-trigger and COBRA/coverage impacts could apply. Also need to know whether Ahmed will be a W-2 employee from abroad prior to US entry 94 that triggers different withholding and possible contractor treatment temporarily. We must consult tax.

anya.ramos: Counsel guidance requested: can Ahmed lawfully "work" from Pakistan for Redwood while on H-1B prior to stamping? Generally, H-1B ties to US employment and H-1B status doesn't authorize employment outside US; counsel often advises remote work abroad is allowed by employer if permitted by local laws but H-1B stamping isn't required if he doesn't travel back to US. However the core issue is re-entry. We'll ask counsel for a written memo on risk and whether he can be onboarded remotely and begin task work before stamping.

maria.khan: I uploaded docs to the immigration form and indicated he may need an expedite. Also sent the manager's preference to ship laptop to Pakistan. Form link: https://intranet.redwood/immigration/newhire-remote-start

hr-bot: Submission received: immigration/newhire-remote-start. Ticket #IM-2026-421 created. Counsel will be looped.

anya.ramos: Action items: (1) I will contact counsel for expedite + remote-work memo; (2) Diane to loop payroll/tax for cross-border payroll implications; (3) Oliver to queue laptop shipping with hold tag; (4) Maria to confirm Ahmed's timezone for onboarding sessions and confirm his local address for shipment. Expect updates within 24 hours.

maria.khan: Thanks everyone. I'll wait for counsel note before approving any international payroll start or remote access. Manager ok with delayed activation.

anya.ramos: Note for the packet we'll provide Ahmed: employer letter for consulate, sample DS-160 email, I-9 guidance (options for reverification), benefits FAQ for remote start, and contact list for HR + legal. We'll also include a short tax checklist to collect his foreign address and declared tax residency.

maria.khan: Appreciate it. Will update candidate and keep thread posted. :thumbsup:
